name: gnu-shogi
why: A playable Japanese chess engine, obscure and old-school, though the variant is familiar to most players.

brief.what_it_is: GNU Shogi is a computer program that plays Shogi, the game also known as Japanese Chess. The gnushogi binary is the AI engine: it takes moves and game input and returns its own moves. The GNU project's page says it is only the engine, so you will usually want a GUI frontend. The gnushogi program also includes a text-based UI.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation. It presents the program as a free software (GNU) implementation of a Shogi-playing engine, with documentation on the rules of Shogi and links to general shogi resources.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the search or evaluation internals. It describes a split design: the engine (gnushogi) handles the AI, and separate GUI frontends such as Tagua, Omaha, Kaya, or XBoard provide the board interface. The source distribution also includes the old xshogi frontend for X Window.

commands_seen.context: Opens the GNU Info documentation for gnushogi, one of the ways the page points to for more information about the program.
Opens the man page for gnushogi, the other documentation route the page mentions.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the homepage notes no accounts, hardware, or runtimes. The gnushogi program itself includes a text-based UI, so it can be played directly in a terminal. For a graphical board, the page suggests installing a separate GUI frontend: Tagua (KDE, stopped development several years ago, still maintained at Debian), Omaha (Gtk2 UI, supports Shogi and other games), Kaya (small KDE successor to Tagua, development seems stalled), or XBoard (GNU project, but 1.4.0 cannot talk to it; patches are in the development version). The source distribution also includes xshogi, a very old X Window frontend. Source tarballs are on ftp.gnu.org, with a test-release area on alpha.gnu.org.
brief.standout: It is a free, decades-old Shogi engine from the GNU project, shipped as a separate AI engine with a text UI and a catalogue of external frontends rather than one bundled GUI. The page is candid that the frontends are dated and that the engine is just the engine.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest release on the GNU FTP index is gnushogi-1.4.2.tar.gz, dated 2014-02-17. Earlier releases are 1.4.1 (2014-01-16) and 1.4.0 (2012-03-25). The homepage still names an active maintainer, Yann Dirson, and says development is a volunteer effort, and the page itself carries a 2026 update stamp. Whether the project is actively developed is not clear from these sources.
brief.caveats: The homepage notes that the XBoard frontend cannot talk to 1.4.0 and that the fix is only in the development version. The suggested GUI frontends are dated: Tagua has stopped development, and Kaya seems stalled. The text UI and the xshogi X frontend are the only options with no extra install. The page describes the work as a volunteer effort, and I found no evidence of recent releases. The homepage is part of gnu.org, and the README says the GNU project page itself was last copyright-dated 2013. The page does not state platform support.
quotes: GNU Shogi is a computer program that plays the game of Shogi, also known as Japanese Chess.
GNU Shogi proper is only the AI engine, and you will likely want to use a GUI frontend to be more comfortable.
The gnushogi program does include a text-based UI if you're into this sort of things, and the source distribution also includes the (very) old xshogi frontend for the X Window system.
